title: Designing Cell-Type-Specific Regulatory DNA with Guided Discrete Diffusion
claim: A pretrained generative model is steered at sampling time by tree search over candidates using surrogate rewards, yielding specific designs.
layout: 2 panels; left training and reward model, right numbered tree-search loop with dashed feedback arrows
description: The figure has two panels. Panel (a), on the left, shows how a class-conditioned discrete diffusion model is trained. A grey box lists the ENCODE registry of regulatory elements (3.2 million human and mouse DNA sequences, with regulatory classes). Next to it, a fully masked sequence passes through a neural-network icon, becomes a partially masked sequence, and ends as an unmasked colored nucleotide sequence. Below this, a sequence-to-activity model scores activity across cell types. Cell icons, DNA icons and activity tracks lead to a MinGap reward formula (mean on-target minus max off-target activity). Panel (b), in a rounded box on the right, shows Monte Carlo tree diffusion. Circular nodes z_T, z_T-1 and z_T-2 form a tree of masked sequences. Seven numbered steps (select, expand, predict, score, prune, update archive, backpropagate) are marked by arrows, checks and red crosses. Dashed black arrows return rewards to parent nodes and to the archive. Colored nucleotide blocks (blue, orange, red, green) draw the eye first.
caption: Overview of DNA-CRAFT. (a) A class-conditioned discrete diffusion model is trained on the ENCODE registry of naturally occurring regulatory DNA. (b) At sampling time, Monte Carlo tree guidance steers the pre-trained class-conditioned diffusion model using cell-type-specific rewards.
abstract: AI-driven design of DNA with cell-type-specific regulatory activity is broadly relevant for cell engineering and gene therapy. DNA elements such as promoters and enhancers have gene-regulatory functions that are defined by their DNA sequence and follow a characteristic regulatory grammar. Deep learning models can effectively predict DNA regulatory activity across cell types, but current generative methods often produce DNA sequences that deviate from the native regulatory grammar, increasing the risk of unexpected behavior and off-target effects in real-world applications. Here, we introduce DNA-CRAFT, a method for designing regulatory DNA with high predicted cell-type-specific activity while preserving naturalness. DNA-CRAFT formulates regulatory sequence design as a guided search over a generative model pre-trained on millions of naturally occurring regulatory elements from the human and mouse genomes. Our method enables targeted exploration of the DNA sequence space, efficient evaluation of candidate designs, and explicit suppression of unwanted activity. Across benchmarks spanning human cell lines and primary immune cells, DNA-CRAFT combines high predicted cell-type specificity with strong motif and sequence-composition adherence, achieving favorable results across the evaluated DNA design tasks.
